strategy_title: Autotune XBLOCK Increase Causes Massive Instruction Blowup
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune with large XBLOCK configs (1024–4096) to a small elementwise kernel caused a 5x regression (22.7 µs → 115.3 µs) despite improving occupancy (45.8% → 85.2%) and compute throughput (37% → 93%). The root cause is that the autotune selected a config (block_size=512, waves_per_sm=62) that executed 84.7M instructions vs 6.7M before — a 12.7x instruction blowup — because the grid remained fixed at 32768 (not updated to use lambda meta) while block size increased, causing each thread to process far more elements than intended. The grid launch in kernel_function was never updated from the hardcoded `triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128)` to `lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(xnumel, meta['XBLOCK']),)`, so the grid size stayed at 32768 regardless of the autotuned XBLOCK, causing massive redundant work.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE: fixed grid, fixed XBLOCK
grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)  # = 32768
triton_poi_fused_addmm_tanh_3[grid](arg_0, arg_1, 4194304, XBLOCK=128)
fast_pseudocode:
# CORRECT pattern when using autotune with variable XBLOCK:
# grid MUST be a lambda that reads meta['XBLOCK']
grid = lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(xnumel, meta['XBLOCK']),)
triton_poi_fused_addmm_tanh_3[grid](arg_0, arg_1, xnumel)
# Without this fix, grid stays at 32768 regardless of XBLOCK,
# causing each block to process XBLOCK elements redundantly.
applicable_when: Never apply this pattern (autotune XBLOCK without updating grid to lambda meta). This is always an implementation flaw.
do_not_apply_when: Any time @triton.autotune is used to vary XBLOCK, the grid MUST be updated to `lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(xnumel, meta['XBLOCK']),)`. If the grid remains hardcoded to a fixed XBLOCK value, the kernel will launch the wrong number of CTAs and execute redundant work, causing severe regression.
framework_notes: Triton-specific: when using @triton.autotune with XBLOCK as a tunable parameter, the grid must be a callable (lambda) that reads meta['XBLOCK'], not a pre-computed tuple. The diff shows the grid was NOT updated to use lambda meta despite the plan specifying it — the kernel_function still used `grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)` with the hardcoded 128. This is the implementation flaw that caused the regression.
